correctness.rationale: Antipodal pairs vanish individually, hence a nonpolygonal minimal subset contains at most one element from each such pair. The signed p×q coefficient matrix lies in the rational cyclotomic tensor kernel c_ij=u_i+v_j. Nonconstant row and column potential ranges must each equal one because every c_ij is -1,0,1 and both extremal signs occur; this forces exactly the opposite-sign diagonal rectangles A×B and Ac×Bc, with mixed zero. Kernel additivity on all submatrices supported there proves minimality. If q+2p-1 consecutive cyclic positions were missing, pair e,e+q for 1<=e<=2p-1 imposes opposite weak inequalities on a_r vs a_{r+q}, forcing equality for all nonzero residues and then globally (q invertible mod p), impossible for proper nonconstant A. Conversely remove two prescribed q-step directed-cycle edges, assign indicator A along the resulting two paths, then consistently color each q-column B to omit 1..q+2p-2; nontriviality follows forced even/odd columns. Independent enumeration of all 16,992 nonempty-proper (A,B) in four prime pairs finds exactly q+2p-1 for every maximum; finite test corroborates full general construction, not a proof of it.
